pairs.question: Iusta doloris, Naeuole, causa tui; contra tamen ille quid adfert?
pairs.answer: Neglegit atque alium bipedem sibi quaerit asellum.
pairs.derivation: The narrator (validating Naevolus's complaint about his patron) asks what the patron offers in return: 'contra tamen ille quid adfert?' Kept the preceding 'iusta doloris, Naeuole, causa tui;' as verbatim setup so 'ille' has a referent. Naevolus answers directly in the next line: 'neglegit atque alium bipedem sibi quaerit asellum.' Capitalized 'Iusta' (starts a new sentence after the full stop following 'impleuero.') and 'Neglegit' (now sentence-initial). Answer cut at the first full stop after 'asellum'; what follows ('haec soli commissa tibi celare memento...') turns to a new topic (keeping it secret), so it is excluded.

pairs.question: Utile consilium modo, sed commune, dedisti. nunc mihi quid suades post damnum temporis et spes deceptas? festinat enim decurrere uelox flosculus angustae miseraeque breuissima uitae portio; dum bibimus, dum serta, unguenta, puellas poscimus, obrepit non intellecta senectus.
pairs.answer: Ne trepida, numquam pathicus tibi derit amicus stantibus et saluis his collibus; undique ad illos conuenient et carpentis et nauibus omnes qui digito scalpunt uno caput.
pairs.derivation: Naevolus's whole speech is one plea built around the interrogative 'nunc mihi quid suades post damnum temporis et spes deceptas?' ('what do you now advise me?'). Quoted the entire contiguous speech verbatim as the question; stripped the dangling inline verse number '125' from the end of the 'spes' line. The narrator answers in the next turn: 'ne trepida... never will you lack a pathic friend.' Stripped the dangling '130' from the 'amicus' line. Capitalized 'Ne' (sentence-initial). The semicolon after 'collibus' is not a full stop, so the answer continues to the full stop after 'caput'; cut there before 'altera maior spes superest...' (further elaboration).
